slides.title: Deep Dive into Requires Expressions
slides.prompt: Requires expressions evaluate syntactic requirements at compile time. They can contain simple requirements, type requirements, compound requirements, and nested requirements.

slides.title: Simple Requirement Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in the expression checking for the presence of a clear() method on object x.

slides.title: Type Requirement Syntax
slides.prompt: How do you check that a type T contains a nested typedef or type alias named iterator inside a requires block?

slides.title: Nested Requirement Keyword
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword required to enforce boolean expression checks inside a requires block.

slides.title: Compound Requirement noexcept Check
slides.prompt: Which syntax specifies that an expression must not throw exceptions?

slides.title: Ad-hoc Requires Clause
slides.prompt: Fill in the double requires syntax used for ad-hoc inline constraints on function templates.
slides.codeSnippet:
template <typename T>
void process(T v) ___ requires (sizeof(T) == 4) {}

slides.title: Subsumption & Concept Ordering
slides.prompt: How does the compiler resolve overloads when multiple constrained templates match a function call?
options: The template with the more specific (subsuming) concept/constraint is preferred
It raises an ambiguous call compilation error regardless of constraints
The first template defined in the header file is chosen
The less constrained template is preferred
slides.correctAnswer: The template with the more specific (subsuming) concept/constraint is preferred

slides.title: Combining Requirements with Conjunction
slides.prompt: Fill in the boolean operator to combine two concepts in a single requires clause.

slides.title: Requires Expression Evaluation Result
slides.prompt: What does a requires expression yield at compile time?
options: A boolean constant value (true if valid syntax, false otherwise)
slides.correctAnswer: A boolean constant value (true if valid syntax, false otherwise)
